summary: 随着大模型应用加速落地，网络作为 AI 算力的“大动脉”，其性能与稳定性直接决定训练与推理效率；本论坛聚焦可预期网络2.0的全栈演进，展现阿里云智算网络架构 HPN8.0 的最新进展，发布围绕 Token Performance Network 的高性能交换机、路由器、光模块、网络操作系统 AliNOS 与通信库等关键技术成果；汇聚NVIDIA、博通、小红书、清华大学等生态伙伴与阿里云技术专家，共探 AI 时代的关键技术融合创新，展现阿里云作为 AI infra 网络技术创新者、行业标准制定者和应用部署实践者的行业定位。

paragraphs.speaker: 桂新征

segments.title: 阿里云智算网络：从HPN到Token Performance Network与UPN
segments.summary: 蔡德忠与席永青连续合讲阿里云智算网络演进。围绕推理SLO和Token成本，将高性能训练网络拓展为以KV为核心的多层存储与RDMA网络，介绍前后端融合、QoS和拥塞控制，以及光互联解耦的UPN架构和跨域网络方向。
key_points: HPN通过高基数、低层级与多平面支撑训练；推理进一步关注时延、可用性和单位Token成本。
以KV为核心组织HBM、DDR与SSD缓存层，网络协同计算与存储资源。
前后端网络融合共享带宽，配合租户隔离、QoS与拥塞控制保障服务目标。
将CPU、沙箱、工具和模型运行时纳入共同网络；UPN探索光互联、组件解耦和Scale-across。

paragraphs.speaker: 桂新征
paragraphs.text: 下面进入今天的第一场主题演讲，有请阿里云网络研发负责人蔡德忠，网络研发资深技术专家席永青，为我们带来阿里云智算网络全栈架构演进。掌声有请。

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 各位现场的嘉宾，线上的朋友们，大家下午好。

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 历史的这个车轮滚滚向前，从我们的预训练训推一体到今天2026年，我们进入了AI Agentic 这个时代，推理成为主战场。对智算网络的要求也发生了一个根本性的变化。智算网络的目标正在从优化训练集群的极致性能转向于优化推理集群的token的效能。今天呢，我们也正式发布为 Token效能而优化设计的。新一代的推理集群网络架构，TPN 1.0。

blocks.title: HPN：面向GW级训练集群昀网络架构
blocks.slide_title: HPN：面向GW级训练集群昀网络架构
blocks.speaker: 蔡德忠

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 在讲TPN1.0之前，我们先简单回顾一下我们HPN的网络架构的这些演进。在HPN7.0、8.0的基础上，我们增加了Pro的这个版本，把双上联双平面拓展到四上联四平面，一方面增加了架构的可靠性，但同时。网络的规模在保持6微秒极致延时的情况下，规模乘以4，我们的8.0 Pro架构可以支持100个Pb的带宽，相当于13万卡的800G的带宽的这个接入。

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 我们正在研发的HPN 9.0是针对一个GW的单集群规模。采用了行业内最先进的204.8T交换芯片，1.6T的自研高性能网卡，基于我们自研硅光芯片的6.4T NPO以及液冷，整个集群可以支持400个Pb的带宽，保持6微秒的极致的延时。

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 一方面，我们的智算。这个集群的HPN还在持续的演进，但是进入了2026年，两个数字说明了拐点已到。第一个数字，进入Agent的时代，对Token的消耗量呈指数级的增长。另外一方面，对算力的爆发式的需求也要求整个行业对token的成本要进行极致性的优化，必须至少进行数量级的这个下降。这对于我们AI基础设施网络来说，提出了新的挑战。我们的网络架构设计要有一些根本性的变革，首先是优化目标，前面已经说了，要从优化集群的极致性能转变为在保证推理服务质量条件下的极致成本。

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 从整个网络架构的设计，要从过去以 scale out为中心，转向scale up、scale out和scale across的协同。同时针对这个推理的百万级的上下文，如何构建更加高效的KV的记忆平面。

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 虽然这个训练和PD它都是一个GPU的矩阵计算，但是我们把它打开一看，从网络的视角，二者其实有着根本性的区别。无论是从它优化的目标、核心的指标、流量的模型，都有根本性的不同。训练追求的是训练任务的尽快完成，它的流量模型是周期性的、同步的大象流，对故障的反应是回到上一个Checkpoint。而对于PD来说，追求的是在满足SLO条件下的有效的吞吐，它是一个异步的小象流，同时叠加大象流，而且流量也特别有突发性。

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 哎，对这个网络中的故障、拥塞、这个抖动是极度的敏感，会影响用户的这个体验。从成本的角度，二者具有更大的区别。对于训练来说，成本就是一个capex。为了达到模型的尽快的训练这个效果，很多模型公司这个成本是不计投入的。但是对于PD来说，网络的成本就是token的一个部分，是一个OPEX的成本，是直接关系到AI大模型能够可持续发展的关键。正是因为如此，我们整个网络架构的设计的这个哲学发生了根本性的变化，从追求极致性能转向于性价比，转向于token的效能。

blocks.title: 网络遇到的4个关键命题
blocks.slide_title: 网络遇到的4个关键命题
blocks.speaker: 蔡德忠

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 这种既要保障用户SLO的质量，又要追求这个成本的数量级的这个下降，这种既要又要对我们的网络提出了无比苛刻的要求，我们必须要直面四个关键命题。第一个就是如何。在百万级长上下文的条件下，PD分离这种架构下，怎么样能够构建更加高效的KV Cache的传输平面？第二个就是在云上多租户的条件下。怎么样在出现网络拥塞故障，怎么样保障多租户的任务级的SLO的性能质量的一个保证？

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 第3个就是异构卡在不同的集群，甚至不同的地域，怎么样保持高性能的传输。第四个，当然也是最核心的，怎么样把成本给降下来？

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 哎，回答这些问题，我们的答案就是TPN的网络。TPN它的名字Token Performance Network，就是为Token的效能而设计的新一代的网络，就是回答刚才4个问题而设计的新一代的网络。它有3个关键的数字，或者3个关键的关键词，一个就是KV-centric，就是我们围绕KV的存储、传输、计算进行协同设计，支持高效的多级缓存，支持更加高效的内存传输语义，构建高效的KV Cache记忆平面。

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 第二个关键词就是SLO保障。这个是相当有挑战的一件事情，就是我们在云上这个共享的物理资源的情况下，怎么样通过端到端的QoS、流控、多路径的一些技术，包括通信库的一些技术，怎么样的协同来保障租户之间的隔离的这个效果，保障它的SLO。第三个就是性价比，就是怎么样把成本降下来。我们过去对于训练这个集群，是采用了front end、back end两网分离的这么一个架构。

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 而对于PD，我们做了两网的融合设计。这个对这个流量的这个带宽的需求是根据需要进行分配啊，把这个成本进行大幅度这个降低。对TPN，我们架构设计的理念和HPN是一样的，就是采用行业最先进的交换芯片。相比我们传统的数据中心网络，它的规模有10倍的增加。对于KV Cache，这个带宽能够提升2.5倍，延时降低1/3，这些都是在成本一样的情况下的一个提升。

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 还要提一点，就是我们为了更好的支持异构卡之间的跨地域、跨机群的传输。我们把我们的新一代的骨干网eCore的一些关键技术，像SRv6和IPv6的RDMA进行结合，支持任务级的路径的这个选择，再叠加长距离传输的CC流控，以及高效的这个选择性的重传。可以达到我们跨地域、跨集群的高性能的网络互联。

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 这个TPN HPN它的背后是我们全栈的软硬件的这个协同。和全栈的自研，从我们的eCore51.2T白盒路由器开始，到支持我们TPN。HPN，还有我们UPN的102.4T交换机，以及我们今年正在规模上量的国产102.4T NPO交换机。啊，我们的光互联啊，我们这个自研的这个硅光芯片，400G、800G已经大规模部署。我们在去年发布了3.2T的NPO。

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 今年我们会和我们的行业伙伴们一起。打造这个新型的交换芯片和6.4T NPO紧密集成的新一代的交换机架构。在网卡这一块，我们也是研发了自研的这个RDMA的高性能网卡和机头的DPU的这个网卡，我们叫eSNIC和MOC。

blocks.title: 智算迈入可预期网络2.0时代
blocks.slide_title: 智算迈入可预期网络2.0时代
blocks.speaker: 蔡德忠

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 啊，这是一幅这个全景图，我们有为万卡、10万卡到一个G瓦的设计的。训练推理一体的大规模集群架构HPN。有为Token效能优化设计的TPN。然后就是我们eCore。用于了我们的scale across。当然，还有我们的UPN，这个架构啊。今天呢，我待会儿我的同事会讲。就是为我们的scale up而设计的全解耦的这个scale up的网络架构。

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 最后呢，做一个简单的总结。就是我们在23年8月份上线了我们的HPN7.0架构，把以太网的性能从best effort变到 predictable，这是我们的可预期的1.0时代。今天我们把predictable。从集群这个性能的维度，再到每个用户的。这个质量的这个保障，同时呢优化这个成本，这就是我们pre，这个是我们的可预期网络的2.0这个时代。

paragraphs.speaker: 蔡德忠
paragraphs.text: 最后呢，我还想说，跟我们的合作伙伴们一起，继续共同来促进网络生态的这个发展。

blocks.title: 联讲交接
blocks.speaker: 席永青
blocks.display_note: 蔡德忠在画外交接；镜头中是准备接讲的席永青。正文按实际说话人标注。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 好，大家好，我是席永青。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 刚刚Dennis提纲挈领地把我们这几年的架构演变的发展，尤其是HPN的发展，以及我们对TPN的思考给大家做了分享。那我这儿接下来会详细展开一下我们的。TPN的网络设计的一些细节和思考，以及UPN的部分。那在这之前，因为当时时间比较紧张，我们前面关于HPN我们今年做的一些工作呢，其实没有太展开。啊，这一页我们先看一下就是。过去这几年，就是阿里云的AI的 Network Infra我们都做了哪些事情？

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: HPN大家比较了解了，其实从2023年我们第一代HPN 7.0上线，那个时候在24年我们有SIGCOMM这个Paper的发表，啊大家都知道我们的工作。其实这两年呢我们也有两个比较重要的迭代和升级。一个是HPN 7.0 Pro，还有一个是HPN 8.0 Pro。刚才丹尼斯的PPT里面也写了一个在明年我们可能会上线的一个新的架构是HPN 9.0。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: HPN架构的这个演进啊，它是随着我们这几年AI这个大的时代浪潮，算力的大规模的发展啊，去同步进行的。第一代的HPN7.0其实只有1.6万卡，也其实就是1.6万个400G。然后我们到HPN 7.0 Pro的时候，是3.2万卡的800G。大家都知道，这个这个规模的来源其实是因为几个因素，这也是HPN一开始设计的一个三个重要的理念。第一个点是两层网络，我们希望通过两层网络把整个智算集群的规模做到足够大。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 那这样的话，两层网络它在成本上，在哈希的一些问题的解决上，在时延上都会优势很大。所以我们的第一个设计理念就是用两层网络去解决啊智算集群的问题。那第二个非常关键的点是用High-radix交换机。我们一开始HPN 7.0其实是按照120，120加上就是按照不到256的radix去用的，然后呢，再往后我们会把这个交换机的radix用到512甚至更大，让两层的这个规模可以按照radix 的翻倍呢，它其实是乘4的。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 然后第三个点，第三个HPN设计的核心是多平面，我们在HPN 7.0第一次提出了两平面的设计，后来大家都知道其实业界也都在往更多平面去做，阿里云的HPN 7.0 Pro可以告诉大家，我们是在去年的这个11月12月份，我们就已经4平面的设计已经上线了。然后HPN 8.0，基于102.4T的4平面集群的设计，在今年也已经上线了，所以整个业界大家可以看到从HPN 7.0到HPN 8.0，实际上，它的整个集群的规模是翻了多少倍？

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 是翻了64倍啊。这个数字其实很简单。一个是Radix的增加，一个是平面数的增加，我们能做到这么大的规模，然后这儿HPN 9.0没有画出来，因为刚才Dennis时间比较紧张，他没有把这一块展开，所以我就多说一点。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 那在去年的时候我们提出了UPN架构，这个Scale Up场景设计的面向未来的光互联的全解耦的一个新型的现在叫超节点，我们会将来当它变成一个解耦系统的时候，我们叫它AI Pod，AI Pod的一个Scale Up的系统。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 然后在今年，我们刚才丹尼斯讲到了TPN的这个逻辑，我们的思考逻辑，我们用TPN，Token Performance Network，专门为Agentic时代推理的业务爆发所设计的一个新型的架构。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 稍微展开一下我们在TPN网络设计里面的一些思考和我们的

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 设计里面的一些重点的点。开始讲设计之前，还是先看一下，就为什么我们做这个设计。我这会讲一些具体的细节。那在几年前，当GPT3.5出来的时候，一直到GPT4吧，大家更多还是把AI当做一个聊天工具去用，那聊天工具在推理过程中，它跟对infra的要求体现在它跟人的交互上。也就是说它的Workload类型主要是人眼去看，然后人去交互、去反馈的这个过程。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 所以有比如说3秒的首字，以及说可能1秒钟20多个，甚至最多到50多个字的这个字符的这个吞吐。那但是，从去年啊，这个CC时刻开始，发现agent的这个能力越来越强。Agent的workload跟原来人去交互的workload就完全不一样，它是一个工具的调用，就token的input和output都是通过tools去交互的，tools是不需要人眼的阅读速度的啊，它非常的快。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 第二呢是说它的执行和交互的上下文很长。基本上是我们就是这这个图里面我们看到的啊，人的交互过程可能最多到这个百K的级别，但是Agent的交互可以到兆级别。这么长的上下文也是需要小时级别的任务啊，能做到这一点的，所以它的执行时间更长，它的上下文更长，并且呢有更严格的SLA。这个SLO就是我们要达到的 TTFT和TPOT的一个目标。那这里呢，最关键的指标其实是TPOT，也就是说在Decode阶段能吐出字符的这个效率和速度越高越好。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 这样的话，你去完成一个Agent任务。它花的时间就会越少。那在整个这个系统过程中，我们看到就是AI Infra要面向刚才讲的这样一个范式去做新的设计。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 那第二个一点是什么？就是整个Agent Workload，还有一些系统架构层面的一些挑战。比如说我们将来的很多节点其实都会变成rack节点，现在叫超节点啊，将来也可能会变成AI pod。就是在这样一个更大带宽的系统域的范围内呢，有一些流量就在这个系统域内就完成了。比如说EP的流量，比如说TP的流量。那这样的话，在推理的过程中，我一个rack里面大部分的流量自己完成之后呢，去出来到rack外面需要跟其他rack 进行交互的流量就变成比如说KV cache，比如说要做模型分发等等。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 那这些流量它有可能没有那么大，那我们机尾的这些网络设计，尤其在超节点这种或者说叫 AI pod的这种rack系统里面。就可能有一些浪费啊，那我们怎么刚才又提到说推理的成本要求又非常高，那我们怎么去权衡这一点呢？这个是网络中在整个系统设计里面要考虑的另外一个点。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 第三个，第三个实际上是KV Cache啊，这个是今年尤其我们做。Agentic这个时代Agent 的infra层面，大家会讲的最多的一个话题。整个LLM，就是Model Runtime的整个过程中，有Prefill的节点，然后有Decode的节点，Decode的节点其实又分为Attention和FFN。那在这个过程中，尤其是 attention部分的这个KV cache的加载，其实对于计算量的这个节约是非常关键的。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 如果你一个很长的上下文的内容，你没有去命中cache，你的KV cache没有拉过来，意味着说你需要重新去算它。当我刚才讲的这么长的上下文啊，1兆的上下文，将来有可能更长，以及说你要去算的时候，你所消耗的这个TTFT的时间，在算力上和在SLO上其实都是不能达标的。那我们一定要把KV Cache的命中率提上去，网络在这其中起到一个非常关键的作用，就是你需要设计足够好的系统，让KV Cache的传输能够很快的达成，让KV Cache的命中率能提上去。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 如果KV Cache的命中率提升15%，就意味着你有15%的Prefill的算力是可以释放出来的。那这些算力拿出来之后，它就可以拿来做推理。所以命中率的提升本质上就是。整个TCO推理TCO的一个下降。那所以推理的成本在这个中间就非常的关键。那网络在其中KV Cache里面能做什么事情呢？

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 这个我后面也会讲到，在TPN里的设计。还有另外一点，就是系统架构设计里面，我们都知道面向未来有可能有其他的一些分离的方式，这些分离的方式主要是为了平衡TPS。per watt，以及TPS per user。在这个过程中呢，就是把attention和FFN分开，这也是业界在在研究和部署的一个新的方向。那这种方式意味着什么呢？意味着说你既然要把它分开，就意味着说你实际上需要把它连起来。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 分开的效率是为了让专用芯片的效能发挥到最大，但是你会带来一个代价，就是你增加了中间传输的这个时间。那传输的时间怎么把它降下来，怎么让它传得更快、效率更高，这个也是网络整个系统里面要去面临的。另外一个关键点，也就是说，高性能网络的在这个层面所扮演的本质是说，用高性能的网络互联去换取专用计算的效率，而去提升整体的TPS。

blocks.title: TPN：为Agent时代设计的新型网络架构
blocks.slide_title: TPN：为Agent时代设计的新型网络架构
blocks.speaker: 席永青

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 所以呢，就是从上面的这些点，从新型的workload的分析，以及说会面临的这些挑战来看，那整个推理的TPN系统的设计，不管是说面向今天的Scale-out这张网络，还是Scale-up这张网络，还是更大范围的Scale-across，我们其实都有3个，3个非常关键的点要去做，第一个就是高效的KV Cache。在阿里呢我们用Stellar的RDMA在存储上已经经过了多年的部署，从Solar到Stellar这个协议。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 所以在如何通过？高效的针对KV Cache定制和研发的RDMA的协议，将HBM、Memory、SSD去构成高效的多级的KV Cache，这个是TPN里面要做的第一个关键的事情。然后第二个是。我刚才提到这些像AI Rack、像超节点、将来的AI Pod，它本身在推理里面也是一个很大的域。那。我们的Scale-out网络到底要不要、要多大？那这里我们的一个做法就是把scale out和front end的网络合并到一起，合并到一起之后呢，让东西向的流量和南北向的流量在需要的时候可以share这个网络带宽。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 比如说现在大部分的这个KV cache 的流量都走的是机头的网络。那走机头网络，可能对于KV Cache来说，影响它的TTFT时间了。那怎么办呢？我如果把机头和机尾的带宽share到一起，KV Cache就可以用到更大的带宽。那这个是我们做的第二个点。第三个点就是在新型的。TPN AI pod这种大带宽的以太网互联里面要去将。推理过程中的EP流量以及PD分离的流量，甚至将来的AF分离的流量，要做到超低的时延和更大带宽的更高效率。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 这个是。我们想到整个TPN的网络里面，我们其实要做的三个关键的事情。

blocks.title: TPN 网络：为 Token 的生产效率与性价比而设计的新型数据中心网络
blocks.slide_title: TPN 网络：为 Token 的生产效率与性价比而设计的新型数据中心网络
blocks.speaker: 席永青

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 那把它放到一起，我们一个TPN的数据中心里面会有哪些东西呢？首先会有Model Runtime，Model Runtime是什么？就是Token in、Token out。它这个系统里面，你给它输入的，Token的网关给它输入的是你的Prompt，是你的上下文，然后它经过大模型的运算之后，给你输出的是Output。所以这个Model Runtime的系统里面包括了GPU，包括CPU，其实也包括了更关键的就是KV Cache。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 那KV Cache这个库我们怎么去做？现在大家都讲我们有L1、L2、L1.5、L3、L3.5等等，那这些多级的KV Cache在网络里面，每一级之间，这个漏斗应该漏多大的带宽过去，这个带宽的设计上是成本是更优的，以及说它的时延比较低，带宽足够，这个其实就是一个关键的问题。那我们通过高性能的RDMA 把不管是计算GPU上的SSD。还是计算节点上的DDR、HBM，以及说可能还需要将CPU服务器和专门的存储服务器上的SSD和DDR 都组成一个大的一个capacity。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 同时我会把另外一些在Agent使用过程中需要调用到计算，需要使用沙箱，需要快速起容器，去调用工具的这部分的资源呢，也放到同一张网络里面。这就是TPN这张网络跟其他网络不一样的地方。我们都知道HPN里面其实我们专注设计的就是把GPU的参数面给连到一起，让参数的计算的效率达到最大。啊，这张图上我们看到了TPN。不一样的地方说，我们是把整个推理过程中的所需要的Model Runtime它的KV Cache以及说它的工具调用的这些所有的组件都放到一张网络里面，啊，让它能够更高效的去产生Token啊。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 这个图可能没那么清楚，这是我们在网络设计上针对TPN做的几个设计。第一个是说我们把机头网络就是把融合机头网络和机尾网络的这张网络的规模做得更大。相比传统的这个前端网络的规模，我们能做到10倍。这个10倍是什么意思呢？就是前端网络，我们把KV Cache和GPU的机头以及部分GPU，有一些GPU可能通过机尾都接到这个前端网络里面，让KV Cache的访问的带宽。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 足够大，这个规模的池子可以足够大，我们可以做到啊，单个Pod可以做到2.6万个400G。然后同时，这个网络里面我们也可以把一些有机尾的，比如说有8个400G或者4个400G甚至更多机尾网络的这个GPU呢，把机尾单独连起来。那当你需要通过机尾去访问KV Cache的时候，我们可以通过上面的SRv6到存储KV Cache所在这个Pod里面啊，这样的话就是我刚才说了，我们把带宽，把这个KV Cache所需要的带宽给做大，这个是带宽做大的一个逻辑。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 然后第3个是我们会把通用计算，把所需要的容器啊、沙箱啊、CPU的计算资源也接到这个集群里面，也放到这个TPN的集群里面，让这些工具调用。的流量和它的访问都能够在一个数据中心和一套架构下完成闭环。整个端到端流量其实很复杂，就是推理网络从Model Runtime到KV Cache到工具调用，这些流量其实是非常复杂的，比我们原来说的HPN里面的机尾参数面的流量复杂得多。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 有一些并行的流量可能在机内，但是有一些并行的，比如说EP流量，它可能会出来。不管是Prefill还是Decode阶段，在这个TPN网络里面需要做比如说EP流量的交互，那还有一些模型的加载，因为推理过程中有可能用模型A，也有可能用模型B，然后不同用户资源需要动态去调整，所以模型加载的流量也会在里面，PD传输的流量会在里面。KV Cache的流量会在里面，工具调用的流量会在里面，所以整张网络的这个QoS和端到端的一些CC和流控就非常重要。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 所以我们又回到前几年说的HPN网络，或者叫参数面的网络里面，我们很干净，它就是各种并行的流量，但是今天到TPN的网络里面，它又会变得非常复杂。流量在数据中心里面，跟以往的复杂度完全不一样。此外呢，为了让这个整个这个推理的资源调度更加协调，因为一个数据中心的推理资源，Prefill和Decode它可能不是完全match的，可能需要跟另外一个数据中心进行PD分离的这个传输，或者说我有一些KV的一些大的一些KV 需要transfer到另外一个数据中心去。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 那我们做了另外一个，就是IPv6的RDMA Scale-across，可以去跨集群跨地域的去实现高性能网络的互联，这是超大的规模。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 好，那后面再讲一下UPN，UPN是我们去年提出的

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 架构，我们看一下整个Scale-up其实从超节点正在走向AI Pod，为什么呢？首先就是我们今年已经有2~3T的模型。是已经变成我们业界的主力了。那下一代模型会是多少呢？这个我们也不好判断，但是预计可能在5~10T。再加上我们上下文的持续增加。所以呢，这个1兆上下文有可能会变成3兆、5兆等等。那在这个前提下，我们也可以看到，就就是今天的超节点它会遇到什么问题？

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 首先就是这种大卡的国外的高端卡的超节点在一个七十二卡的域内。它有20T的HBM。这20T的HBM如果说放了一个10T的模型，这个10T的模型用比如说用FP8去做量化，那刚好是一半一半，因为你一半放模型，一半放KV cache，这个10T是可以的。但是如果这个模型你要放到国产的64卡或者72卡的AI Rack里面，它其实就不够了。啊，你可能能放一个5T的模型。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 那这样的话，尤其是在国产的xPU未来面向未来的2到3年的模型去做推理的话，它一定会遇到瓶颈。也就是说，我们现在的这个超节点。必然要走向光互联的这种AI Pod，要打破算力和HBM的瓶颈。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 那就是天下没有免费的午餐，就是说我们要把一个rack变成更大规模的，比如250、256、288，甚至一开始是更大的这样一个AI pod，它会遇到哪些问题呢？突破距离限制之后一定要上光，那上光了之后，我们一定会问说这个成本到底怎么办？成本的问题怎么办？然后这个还有说光的这个稳定性的问题怎么办？其实这个我们在去年也回答过这个问题啊。从另外一个角度来讲，我们做这件事情的好处是说，这种这种AI rack它的高密的复杂的系统可以被新的这种光互联，把复杂系统的硬件的成本和复杂度和稳定性给它解决掉，我们解耦了之后，它的box的设计、硬件的设计就不会那么复杂。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 但是光的部分会更有挑战一些。所以我们去年的这个UPN架构实际上是一个从小机重回x86的一个全解耦的一个架构啊。主要是通过低成本的光互联加软件和网络协议层面的高冗余，加交换机的大Radix，去通过一层交换机，简单的低成本的把。一个大带宽的GPU的域给连起来。最多可以连到从256到比如说1152个xPU，都可以做到，这个跟一层交换机，它交换机本身的radix有关系。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 我们在其中做的有几个重要的工作，一个是光互联这部分的这个能力，我接下来一页里面会讲。然后第二部分是我们也做了。在网计算啊，这个里面我没有写出来。其实我们今年在网计算有了很大的一些一些进展，大家也看到了，我们发表了这个IFAC的一些标准。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 通过这样一个系统，我们去把整个超节点解耦，去盒式化，去降低节点的复杂度，去降低硬件上的成本。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 那同时光的这个成本会上升，那这儿就也跟大家分享一下我们在光互联技术上的一些进展。核心技术，我们有两个。第一个是说……嗯，左边这个图就我们一种新的封装形态啊，大家都知道我们现在有FRO，有LPO，然后还有NPO和CPO。那在在去年我们跟博通一起合作，提出了这个新的一种封装方案，叫 IPO，Near Package Optics。那这种封装形态是介于NPO和CPO之间，它比NPO的封装距离更贴近于主芯片。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 啊，它的损耗会更低。它的信号质量会更好，同时它又没有CPO这么紧密的耦合系统。然后大家都知道CPO上的问题，如果我要去做一个CPO的话，把它封装到一起，多厂商的合作是更复杂的，本身的工艺挑战也是很大的。所以IPO的方式可以很大程度上去中和CPO的。性能的优点，但又可以去解决它的复杂度的一些痛点，那又会比NPO的这个性能会更好。然后这个IPO的系统，其实我们已经完成了，大家可以到我们的那个展台上去看。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 另外就是3.2T的NPO和6.4T的UPO啊，6.4T我们叫Ultra Performance Optics，我们在业界已经有标准推出来了，然后明年的年终我们大概就可以测试，可以来看。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 我们整个如果把整个阿里云，我们今天说推理，如果把整个阿里云的网络，把阿里云的所有的计算资源看成一台大的计算机的话，那这个推理的系统会长得是这样。首先最上面是我们通过eCore专门为推理和AI网络所构建的一张eCore Scale-across网络，就是跨地域地通过RDMA的这个长距离的RDMA 的能力，把多个数据中心给连接起来。然后每个数据中心里面我们有TPN的网络，然后TPN的网络是我刚才讲的KV Cache啊，然后Scale-out和Frontend的融合，等等这些能力，去高效的去。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 提升KV Cache的能力，然后在推理中有端到端的QoS和CC的能力。再加上我们针对。推理的场景以及训练的场景要去做的这个更大规模scale up的AI pod啊这样一个完整的系统，会是大家看到的我们面向推理时代，我们要构建的所有的3个主要的这个架构

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 所构成的系统。好，最后呢就是。一开始也有人问说，这个可预期网络1.0是什么？为什么我们今天讲2.0好，那1.0其实可预期网络是阿里云这几年的云栖大会。我们都知道我们每届都是可预期网络论坛。那以前没有标号1.0，是因为今天我们有新的进展，我们针对这个推理的场景有新的设计，然后网络的目标也发生了变化。这个刚才Dennis也讲到了，所以可预期网络我们正式把它引进到2.0。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 1.0的时候，在智算时代，我是面向训练去把一个数据中心把它构成一个大的计算机，其中有两个关键的点，第一个是说我们要让规模变化之后的算力的性能保持线性。不要让它下降太多，这个就是网络在推理过程中的做的第一件重要的事情。第二件重要的事情是说万卡和10万卡的单任务在训练过程中，我们不能让它因为网络的各种各样的原因所产生failure，让它训练。

paragraphs.speaker: 席永青
paragraphs.text: 被中断，这个是在可预期网络 1.0时代我们所做的重要的工作。那今天再往后，当推理的规模10倍、100倍的增长时候，我们必须要跨越到下一个时代，我们必须要面向可预期网络2.0去做整体架构的设计。可预期网络2.0就是在。推理的SLO满足的前提下，我们要通过低成本、高吞吐的网络能力去服务这个KV Cache，然后在EP啊、PD分离，甚至AF分离、模型分发等等任务调度这样一个系统下去提供更好的满足要求的SLO，以及更好的网络性能和更低的网络成本。

segments.summary: Asad Khamisy从AI工作负载的通信需求出发，讨论Scale-up、Scale-out和Scale-across所需芯片能力。结合Broadcom交换与网卡产品，分析带宽、基数、PHY、共享缓存互联和封装散热的扩展限制，并介绍分解式封装、CPO与光互联方向。
key_points: 不同并行方式在Token时延、吞吐和网络成本上形成不同权衡。
芯片扩展受I/O边界、PHY布局、片内数据路径、缓存互联和散热制约。
高速电与光接口需要联合考虑信号完整性、功耗及制造良率。
CPO与光学Scale-up还涉及可维护光纤连接、封装结构、冷却和热膨胀。

paragraphs.speaker: 桂新征
paragraphs.text: 我们进入下一个话题，下面有请Broadcom核心交换事业部高级副总裁兼总经理Asad带来《赋能超大规模AI：构筑高带宽网络的芯片技术创新》。掌声有请。

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Very much. I am very happy to be here today and talk to you about the challenges we are facing in scaling the switch element. For the AI infrastructure.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So the talk is going to be focused on what happens when you scale the switch, what are the challenges we face inside the silicon, inside the package, in the IO and so on.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And some of the speakers before me touched actually on some of these challenges. Okay.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay, so when we look at AI, we look at it as a very large distributed computing system. So if you look at the cloud, the cloud was more about virtualization, right? You had multiple virtual machines running on the same server.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: You wanted isolation between them. Each virtual machine was a different customer, different application and so on. But when you have a training job, and that training job is very large, it cannot run on a single machine.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: You have to distribute it across large number of machines, and all of them working on the same job. So that's a fundamental difference here. And the way these GPUs communicate with each other is very critical.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So the way you build your network, the way you architect your network is very, very important.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And let me just try with a simple example to illustrate why the network is important. And in this example, one of the popular techniques in scale up, it's called tensor parallel.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Basically, you take your neural network, you take every layer, and you break it down across multiple GPUs. You break your model down across multiple GPUs. Okay. And so if you look at the latency to produce a token, it's really a function of, you know, you have pre-fill and decode and I'm focused

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: mostly on decode because it's the majority of the computation. And so you have latency in terms of accessing the HBM and the compute. And this latency, as you distribute your model across more and more XPUs, each XPU is handling a smaller model, so the latency decreases.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So as we increase the number of GPUs, the latency decreases. But if you look at the network and the red line is showing a two-tier network latency, the yellow line is a single tier network latency.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So the red line represents a higher-latency network, the yellow line is lower latency network because it's a single tier. So as you break your model across more and more XPUs, there is more communication between these XPUs.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And so your latency goes up, the opposite direction of what we saw in HBM and compute. And if we merge those together, what we see here is the green line is the lower latency network, the single tier network.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: What you can see, we can now distribute our model across more XPUs and reduce the time per output token. Okay, that's a simple example using, you know, the assumptions on the bottom here, 400 billion parameter, 576 XPUs.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So that just illustrates why the network is important. Okay?

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: But this is not the only parameter. Latency is not the only parameter. What we want from the AI network, we want it to be scalable to millions of GPUs. Okay, we have seen the previous speakers talking about very large network.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: We want resiliency against link failure, right? If a link fails, we don't want to restart the training job, for example. We want low packet loss because every packet loss translates to a retransmission.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And retransmission is an order of magnitude more latency. than dropping this packet. You want to run at a very high utilization. We see some of our customers running at 90% utilization.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: The cloud was typically running at 60% utilization. So you want to run at very high utilization. And you want low tail latency under load. And why tail latency is important?

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Because in AI, jobs are synchronized. You have bursts going into the network. And so you really care about tail latency more than the system is empty and I'm sending a packet, okay?

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay, and so the way we look at AI network today is, and I think the previous speaker showed a similar model, we look at scale up, which is typically inside the rack. And typically it's a memory fabric, but not always.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Memory fabric. Then you have a scale out where we put multiple of those racks inside the building typically up to we have seen 128,000 XPUs and when you run out of power in the building, you use more buildings that are geographically distributed, and so you have what we call scale across network, connecting them.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And the distance here can be very large. It can be 100 kilometers. We've seen even 300 kilometers with some customers.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So at Broadcom we support building AI network, okay? We provide the technology components, hardware and software, at a very accelerated rate across switching, PHY, optics, all the components that you need.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: At a very high pace of innovation to enable you to build the best network for your application. Okay, we provide you these tools and you build your network. So we have Tomahawk Ultra is our 50 terabit switch for scale up and for HPC market.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: It is demonstrated. 237 nanoseconds of latency. Okay, so it is approaching some of the best latency out there. It also supports collectives. And a 256 scale-up domain, okay, compared to today's 72 scale up domain with Tomahawk Ultra and get to 256.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Tomahawk 6 is the only 100 terabit per second switch in volume production today. Okay, that is used today. Some of our customers actually use it for scale up, and some of them use it for, mostly it's a scale-out product, but some customers use it for scale-up because of the high radix 512.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Here, Jericho 4 is our solution for scale across, giving you deep buffer to minimize packet loss. Because the queuing latency is order of magnitude less than the retransmission latency.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: That's why it's important. Okay, and it is not like Jericho 4, every packet going through it, go to the deep buffer. It is not. Okay, we have on-chip buffers that move data very efficiently and with very low latency.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And only when there is congestion, instead of dropping the packet, we can store the packet in the buffer. and that's much more efficient than retransmitting the packet all the way from the source, so that's why it's important.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And then we have the NIC, Thor Ultra, an 800-gig NIC. It is the first Ultra Ethernet Consortium-compliant NIC, with programmability for what we call the PDS layer, the layer that does congestion control, load balancing and so on.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And we also provide an IP called SerDes to our XPU customers. And today, some of them have started deployment at large volume where they deploy our IP to do Ethernet for scale up, memory interconnect.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And their scale up. is 2000 domain, not 72, because that's what Ethernet allows you to do. We also provide the software component. We're very active in SONiC, SAI and RoCE Stack as well.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay, so let's now get down to the switch element, which is the main component in the network. And what happens when you want to scale the switch element? When you want to scale the radix, we're going today at 512, tomorrow we're going to be at 1024, and want to scale the switch bandwidth as well,

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: right? From 50T to 100T to 200T and so on. What happens when you scale? The die size goes up, the package size goes up, the interposer size goes up, the interconnect size is the most important parameter for switch design.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: The interconnect size goes up. The power supply, the power density, the thermal density become major challenges. So when you scale the switch, all the physical parameters scale, go up in complexity.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay? So AI makes radix and bandwidth growth very valuable. However, the challenges of integration become very, very large. Okay, and let's talk about those challenges right now.

blocks.title: Tomahawk5
blocks.slide_title: Tomahawk5
blocks.speaker: Asad Khamisy

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So this is Tomahawk 5. It's a monolithic die. It is the lowest power 50 terabit switch today. It is measured by independent parties as being 50% lower power. When Dennis talks about OPEX, OPEX is about power, right?

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: If you save 50% power, you save 5,000 dollars over five years. And when we went to Tomahawk 6, because we wanted to maintain the shared buffer architecture, we wanted to maintain the features for scale-out, we had to go to multi die.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And we also. came with a solution which provides you 512 by 200 gig, but also 1024 by 100 gig, which is what mainly China is using. across all our customers in China, you are using Tomahawk 1024 by 100 gig.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So we give you this flexibility. And you can see here the package size. didn't increase much. Why is that? Because of the efficiency of the design. If you compare Tomahawk 6 package size with existing 50-terabit switches in the market, it is a smaller package size at 100 terabits per second.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So that efficiency is what allows us to scale.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Now let's talk about the key switch component. When you build a switch, what do you have inside the switch? Essentially, you have the die, which is the silicon. You have I/O to receive and send packets.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: You have a data path to take that traffic and push it into a buffer. And we use shared buffer because it's the best approach. to give you the best traffic management, the best quality of service.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So you have I/O, data path, and packet buffer. And inside the package, we support different types of I/Os. We support pluggable optics, co-packaged copper, co-packaged optics, and integrated optics as well.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And today, first time I hear the term IPO, which I'm going to talk about later because we call it the same name.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay, so let's talk about I/O. So I/O speed. I/O speed was, five or six years back, 25 gigabit NRZ, and we supported optics and copper in the same SerDes. And that's how standards were defined, IEEE standards or OIF standards.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: 50 gigabit, 100 gigabit and 200 gigabit maintain this property. of the same SerDes modulation for both copper and optics. However, it is changing when we go to 400 gig serial.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Next year, we're going to build products with 400 gig. And what we realize is for optics, 400 gig PAM4 matches very well with optics because optics is going with PAM4. And if you want to support LPO or NPO, or LRO, you want to match the optic modulation, and that's PAM4.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: However, for copper, When you run at PAM4, your Nyquist frequency is 100 gigabit per second. You cannot go too far. Your losses are very high. So PAM6 is what's emerging as the technology for 400 gig over copper today.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And we believe we can support 400 gig PAM6 inside the rack and have a 1-meter cable. Okay。

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay, let's talk about I/O technology. So when you build a switch, The number one challenge. is the beachfront. How do you put all these SerDes lanes? That's the number-one challenge, okay?

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So if you look at when we had 256 lanes, 25.6 terabits per second, we put the PHYs around the perimeter, east, west, north, south. You can see it. When we double the number of lanes, we had to stack those cells.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: We had to put two rows and two columns next to each other. And the challenge here is how you escape those cells through the package. But when we go to 1024, like Tomahawk 6 100T that you're using, When you have 1,024 lanes, you cannot do it anymore.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay, so this is where we had the PHY tile, and you can see how we expanded the beachfront of the switch. Okay, so this is what we did in Tomahawk 6. We will continue to come with innovations to enable us to integrate more and more lanes going forward.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay, datapath. Datapath, so what's happening in process technology? If you look at TSMC today or any fab, process technology. What they call the backend or the metal stack, the metalization is not really changing.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: The number of routing layers you have. is either the same or maybe two more. Okay, the resistance and capacitance of those wires is actually becoming worse. Okay, and you're not getting much speed improvement.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Which means if I want to build a datapath, the number of wires I need to send a terabyte, I need to double that number. So that introduces significant challenges in managing power density, thermal density and routing of those wires.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So that's a fundamental change the silicon industry, switching industry is facing going forward.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay, let's look at the packet buffer. So typically, when you have a packet buffer of, we have 300 megabytes, right? You don't build it from one piece, okay, because of speed limitations.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Your configuration is roughly in a few megabytes. So you need many, many of those small memories working together to behave as one single shared buffer. And so when you double.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Your write bandwidth from X terabit to 2X terabit, when you double your read bandwidth from X terabit to 2X terabit, You have no choice but to double the number of instances.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And so if you look at it, it's really a quadratic increase in interconnect and memory. and that is significant. it's not a linear increase, it's a quadratic increase. when the process technology is not giving you more speed.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: is not giving you more density. The memory technology pretty much remains similar from one process node to another process node. So that's a fundamental challenge we're facing.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay, now let's, we talked about the die, the I/O, the data path, the memory, the packet buffer. Let's go to the package now. Okay? So inside the package, if we talk about I/O technologies, We have co-packaged optics, where we co-package optics on the package substrate.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And we also co-package copper. So Broadcom productized co-package optics about two years ago. It was deployed by several customers, not at a high scale, relatively low scale, but we got experience with it.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: This is Tomahawk 6 Davisson, 1024 DR4 optics. Actually, 512, sorry, 512 DR optics. And now we said, okay, so how do we scale co-packaged optics? You want to put more optics, how do you do it?

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: You continue to increase the package substrate, the challenges you're facing are significant, okay? So this is an innovation Broadcom came with. It's called integrated copper attach, ICA, the previous speaker called it IPO.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: This innovation allows you to decouple The integration of copper and optics from the package itself streamline the manufacturing flow. This is something we're bringing up in Tomahawk 6 right now.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And then OCI is the technology we came with for scale up. I'll touch on it briefly.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay, so integrated copper attach. This is the technology I just talked about. This is the package that we deliver to our customers. And I think you have a demo here in your exhibition.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So this one, what you see in blue, the blue color there, is a socket that you buy from one of our three suppliers. You put it here and you attach this card on it. And this card you can manufacture separately.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: You can build it with copper, you can build it with optics, you can put whatever connector you want. It decouples the package, the package itself from the card that has the co-packaged optics and co-packaged copper. It becomes like an optical module, basically.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay, so that's the advantage here.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay, these are co-packaged optics products. This is our Tomahawk 6. Davisson Meta published a report showing 1 million hours of no link flaps, so very high reliability. Today they're up to 50 million hours without any link flap.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay, so we're maturing our CPO technology more and more, and next year we'll get it to production. And we also have, uh, you know, Broadcom, we believe in open platform, not only open standards, open platform.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So we enable our partners to build their own package with Tomahawk 6 and offer it to their customer where their customer can put their own optical module.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay, let's talk about some of the challenges in co-package optics. I'm going to talk about three key challenges. One is the interface between the electrical and optical die.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: This interface is very critical, especially signal integrity. Whether you're using hybrid copper bonding or micro bump bonding, both of them you're running about 40 to 50 micron pitch and the signal integrity today in 200 gig is a major challenge.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And imagine what's going to happen when we go to 400 gig here. The second challenge is really SMT, how you assemble those systems on the board at high temperature, how you do reflow.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So you need a detachable fiber technology. You need to have a miniature connector where you can detach and attach the fiber. And finally, and the most important thing for CPO, This is what we've been working on at Broadcom.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: We've been setting up a manufacturing line, manufacturing at scale, manufacturing at a very high yield. Okay, you see here the equipment at Broadcom assembling the lid around the package for our Tomahawk 6 CPO.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So manufacturing at scale is going to be the major challenge.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay, now next I'm going to talk about some of the technologies we're bringing up to enable increasing the scale-up domain, how we go from 64 to thousands of XPUs and where we face the issue of reach.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Copper is good within the rack, right? You can go two meters, maybe three meters. But when you have thousands of XPUs in a scale-up domain, you need multiple racks, your distance is longer.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: So Broadcom invented OCI, Optical Compute Interconnect,

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: and we partner with a number of companies, you see them here, to establish an MSA standard. We have this technology already implemented. We are proving the concept right now at large scale.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And we're going to deploy it in future products. This technology allows you to achieve the same power as copper, similar cost to copper and enables you to go for a much longer distance.

blocks.title: Total Link Power and Reach Comparison - 200G
blocks.slide_title: Total Link Power and Reach Comparison - 200G
blocks.speaker: Asad Khamisy

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And here's a table comparing the different technologies. So if you have XPU and switch, they're connected with DAC on one side, DAC on the other side, you're 7 picojoule per bit.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: 7 picojoule, 7 milliwatt per gigabit, 2 meter reach. You can add a retimer, active copper, and you can get to 5 meter with 14 picojoule per bit. And integrated OCI, that technology I talked about, optical compute interconnect, will allow us to actually close the gap with copper, but give you half a kilometer of distance.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: It all depends. on our ability, us and the rest of the industry, to bring this technology at volume. And once you bring it at volume, it will enable us to build very large clusters cost efficiently.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: You see the CPO and the pluggable power and reach as well.

blocks.title: Datacenter Advanced Packaging – Four Fronts of Innovation
blocks.slide_title: Datacenter Advanced Packaging – Four Fronts of Innovation
blocks.speaker: Asad Khamisy

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay. And these are some of the challenges in the package itself. So we talked about the die, we talked about the IO, and we also have significant challenges in the package.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: As you go to 3D technology, your coefficient of thermal expansion now becomes super complex. You have the package substrate expanding one way, the interposer expanding another way.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: The first. floor of the die expanding one way and the other floor expanding a different way. So that becomes a major challenge we need to overcome. These are some of the challenges we need to overcome on the package -- packaging technology itself.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And if we look at our evolution at Broadcom, starting from Tomahawk, Tomahawk 2, Tomahawk 3 to Tomahawk 6, you can see how the package size increased all the way from 55 to 118 in Tomahawk 6 100 gigabit.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Tomahawk 6 200 gigabit, you can see we maintain package size similar to Tomahawk 5 actually.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: Okay, and this graph basically illustrates the industry evolution of how you manage thermals. As our power increases, we're decreasing the theta JA, the thermal efficiency, so that the multiplication of both is constant.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And today we see 1500 watt as the boundary between air-cooled and liquid-cooled.

paragraphs.speaker: Asad Khamisy
paragraphs.text: And finally, I'm just putting this slide about the Broadcom offering for Ethernet. We give you the tools and components to customize for your application.

segments.title: 扩展AI工厂的五大网络基础设施
segments.summary: Rochan Sankar将AI工厂网络划分为Scale-up、Scale-out、Scale-across、Context scale和Scale-in五个方向。介绍NVLink、Spectrum-X、跨站点端侧流控、KV上下文复用及BlueField管理安全基础设施，强调硬件软件协同设计和给定功耗下的Token产出与交互体验。
key_points: Scale-up与Scale-out服务不同并行通信，需协同网卡、交换机与运行时。
多平面、较少网络层级、自适应路由和拥塞控制用于提升利用率与故障恢复。
Scale-across强调端侧信用流控，Context scale面向KV缓存与上下文复用。
Scale-in利用DPU承载管理、安全和编排，减少基础设施对计算资源的挤占。

paragraphs.speaker: 赵雨晴
paragraphs.text: 下面有请英伟达AI网络产品副总裁Rochan带来《扩展AI工厂的五大网络基础设施》。掌声有请。

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: It's great to be here, and I'm here on behalf of NVIDIA to talk about the AI infrastructure advances that we believe are key. Purpose-built infrastructure is at the core of what we have built at NVIDIA, specifically for the era of agentic AI.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: And we'll talk about why that is and the various dimensions that we do use co-design in order to optimize the performance of the AI factory overall.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: So, as my colleagues have talked about earlier, agentic AI is an enormously demanding workload. It's in fact the most complex workload that we've seen in the data center overall.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: And in history, actually. This is no longer an operation of simply prompt, conversational output. And it's very fitting that this session is called the Token Performance Network.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: We believe that the ultimate gauge for the performance of an agentic AI data center, of an agentic AI factory, is overall in the token output of that factory. And with agentic workloads, That is basically running loops.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: So we talk about agents that are ingesting context. And then reasoning, observing, acting on them. and being able to connect those to various services and then running those loops over and over again.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: So instead of a single inference operation in this Token Performance Network, we are talking about infrastructure that must support. many tens, maybe hundreds of such operations happening.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: In many cases, at speeds that are much faster than the speed of human conversation or ingestion. Along with this, the agents have to rely on tools and skills to be able to pull that in.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: This relies on leveraging processor as well as the CUDA layer and the models themselves. Binding them together using security and governance. And all of this is backstopped by a large substrate of memory in the AI factory.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: through CPU, GPU, the CUDA layer, the LLM layer and by the network as well.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: So given this agentic AI workload, Why purpose built networks? Well, ultimately, If the overall performance of the AI factory is judged by the throughput and the interactivity, the historical or the traditional Pareto curves that we see, that determine the efficiency of your AI factory.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Ultimately, we want the network technologies that we build here to be able to produce the best possible result in those two vectors for a given amount of power. So keeping the data center footprint of power constant, how can we maximize the throughput?

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: And how can we maximize that throughput for an increasing amount of interactivity? Because both with agentic AI are increasing in both dimensions. And so with that, There are actually five distinct network infrastructure dimensions that we at NVIDIA believe in the extreme co-design of, and in there being unique

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: identities for how those networks are constructed. Scale up is well known. It is the memory fabric, the high performance, ultra low latency memory fabric between GPUs or accelerators to move data between them, between themselves and memory.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: We build this using the NVLink technology, which has demonstrated, in production today and across the global footprint, the lowest-latency, highest performance scale up technology.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Scale out is the technology that allows the establishment of tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of GPUs and accelerators to work in concert in order to scale that AI workload.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Across tenants and across multitude of services. We also have heard about scale across. NVIDIA actually, you know, coined the term of scale across to be able to provide services across a global infrastructure using clusters that may be distributed across regions or across geographies and allowing those workloads to be

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: able to seamlessly be integrated at global scale. But there are two other Network dimensions that I'd like to talk about today. One is context scale. Um, the first presentation today talked about it in great detail.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Agentic actually increases the amount of reuse of KV cache. Because of the speed at which that's generated and the need to not recompute what is very frequently fetched context.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: That context scale now needs to scale almost independently across many tenants and many services. So context scale is another dimension of the network that must factor into your Token Performance Network and in the scaling of the overall bandwidth and resources.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: The second is scale in. With Agentic, the administration and orchestration of services become even more important. Security policy and the provisioning of all of these resources has to be done by some element.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Historically, the CPU would be in charge of that. The CPU has finite bandwidth. And so we are. In this presentation, I'll talk about our BlueField DPU and its ability to act as effectively a scale-in orchestrator, which can supervise bandwidth across all of these network infrastructures that I'm showing today between scale-out, scale-up,

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Even scale across. So there's a purpose for building each of these in order to optimize performance, latency, serviceability, resiliency, and the like. They're not all. The same metrics or KPIs that we are judging for

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: the design of each of these networks. Let me start with scale up and explain how we think about scale up as a network. Today we build the highest-performance scale-up network with NVLink stretching to a domain of 72 within the rack.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: And that's based on the amount of flops that we expect to see operating most in the sweet spot of the frontier models. And that will continue to scale. And ultimately, what we've seen in the data we've collected is that you still want to keep your scale-up domain somewhat contained.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: meaning if scale up starts to get very, very big. The latencies associated with just even transmission. Or in the amount of traffic that could be creating noise across that.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: actually goes to the detriment of the memory fabric semantic that is key to preserving the performance and the latency that you need for very tight tensor parallel and expert parallel communication.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: So the key on scale-up is not just ever-increasing radix. And that's a very important point for design in terms of how we segment the workloads between the scale-up domain and the scale-out domain.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Very much important, especially for Token Performance Network and inference clusters. And you can see from the graph that I'm showing here that ultimately the judge is of what is the best network to use for scale up is on the token output curve.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: What kind of productivity, what kind of throughput can you get with respect to token performance? along the axis of interactivity and so how you do disaggregation, how you move.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: the workload from one element to another. When it's combined on the same NVLink scale-up fabric, what we found is. Significant performance gains versus other off the shelf scale up technologies.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: And this has been measured and verified by third-party analysts and labs. That advantage in scale-up, which is proven, is something that delivers a higher level of AI factory performance.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: at the same power footprint.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Let me talk about Ethernet for a second. Obviously, NVIDIA thinks of Ethernet as a core technology as well in the AI factory. But ultimately, Ethernet has historically and currently.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: has had to carry the burden of serving many markets, and it's built into the semantics of how Ethernet actually works. It has the ability to innovate, but it's effectively a very big ship that we have to try and steer.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Ethernet needs to be purpose built for the scale out function in AI factories. for high performance distributed computing.

blocks.title: Spectrum-X：
blocks.slide_title: Spectrum-X：
blocks.speaker: Rochan Sankar

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Spectrum X, featuring both NIC and switching architectures, is the eminent Ethernet architecture for gigascale AI factories, scaling to hundreds of thousands of GPUs, accelerators, XPUs, In the AI factory.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: with features such as adaptive routing, congestion control, and jitter-free communications that enable significant throughput advantages. We've measured over 60% higher RDMA bandwidth that is possible to get out of the same network versus off the shelf.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Over 2x multi-tenant bandwidth, which is the presence of alternate background noisy jobs or noisy neighbors. And 30% lower jitter. using Spectrum-X technologies. Using the interplay and the co-design between the NIC and the switch to be able to do state-based accounting, link load detection,

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: and ultimately to design a much more responsive scale out network between nodes.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: When we look at the data regarding Spectrum X in the multi-tenant AI factory, what we see is that, and this is using DeepSeek V3 in a training job in a multi-job environment.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: So there's a presence of more than just the training job, but effectively additional jobs in back of it. As we see. the steps through that particular training job and the introduction of additional noise with other background GPUs.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: An off-the-shelf Ethernet solution tends to be able to amplify some of that with respect to the impact on overall step time, the actual job completion time required for that particular training step.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: So that advantage of having 1.9x higher training performance is something that we observe just because of the accounting that is done in Spectrum-X between the endpoint and the switch to be able to optimize for the lowest job completion time.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: I mentioned extreme co-design. A key part of that that is not talked about much is the software. Obviously, NVIDIA invests a great deal in our collective libraries, in our software stack overall.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: In order to assist and provide the frameworks by which inter GPU and accelerator communication is leveraged, and it's widely regarded as the standard for the communications library leveraged in both inference and training.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: As you can see here with Spectrum X Ethernet. We are taking some exemplary operations that are performed in the NCCL library, a gradient all reduce which improves by 2x. Token dispatch improving also by 2x, reduce scatter.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: An increase of 3.5x based on the combination of Spectrum X as well as the NCCL Library. And when parallel matrix multiply actually has to extend beyond the scale up domain into the scale out, as there is sometimes a need to do so, there's a much higher throughput advantage that we get using Spectrum X that we've

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: observed. This is using Nemotron Ultra in terms of pre-training and inference workloads that we've measured.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: So I agree with my other presenters here that scale out and the AI factory itself actually relies on, in the future, the velocity and the reliability of optics. And the differences are clear between a cloud data center historically and an AI factory in that you have much more bandwidth that is being serviced here,

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: and a need for very, very high reliability in the interconnections between

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: nodes in that AI factory. We're proud that NVIDIA has been at the forefront of photonics innovation and that our CPO technology, our silicon with MRM-based capability is one that we have demonstrated and is now coming to market based on 3D stack photonics technology using TSMC CoWoS.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: One of the key advantages of our CPO is the ability to amortize the efficiency and power of the laser across multiple lanes. So effectively we're able to use over, for example, a 1.6 terabit transceiver, the ability to distribute that across multiple 400 gig lanes.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: and therefore reduce the number of lasers that are actually deployed in the data center. This thereby reduces the overall power footprint, which is a significant driver of the tolerance of optics technologies in the increasing size of an AI factory.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: And. As our data has shown us as well, it's a highly reliable technology, being able to support an order of magnitude better time between failures.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: And we're happy to say that that CPO technology, um, based on MRM and TSMC CoWoS is in production now.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Going back to scale out and the typical topologies that we have seen the hyperscale data center evolve through. Obviously, the AI factory relies on a much higher level of connectedness between all of the nodes in the data center.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: So a hierarchical multi-tier top-of-rack spine or leaf spine type of topology, while that served general purpose workloads, it. has its deficiencies in terms of minimizing overall latency from endpoint to endpoint.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Spectrum X multi-rail was sort of the first technology that was introduced a few years ago that actually tried to minimize the end-to-end latency of these workloads by creating rail-based topologies between various nodes.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: This was fundamentally based on the ability of the SuperNics. At the XPU or GPU node, as well as the switches of distributing the traffic.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: We've announced this year Spectrum X Ethernet Multiplane. And Multiplane effectively extends the AI factory scale by a significant amount. It creates within the rails the ability to go across multiple planes using fine-grained bandwidth at the super NIC.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: So you can see in this example with Spectrum X. Each GPU or XPU is effectively able to distribute its traffic across multiple planes. And thereby create the ability to scale to, as I said, 64 times the overall factory scale in as few layers of the network as possible.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: In this example, we're talking about 512,000 GPUs, using a 1.6-terabit scale-out bandwidth per GPU and 102.4-terabit switches.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: So not only does this approach save in the total amount of scale out switches,

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: But importantly, it's an extremely important topology and architecture that maximizes bandwidth and maximizes recovery from loss in the network. What we've observed and measured is relative to a traditional, you know, NIC switch type of topology.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Spectrum-X in that multiplane effectively reduces the detection time for bandwidth loss on any one of those ports and restores recovery to at least a 90%bandwidth within a couple of milliseconds.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: When we measure this at scale at the AI factory level. The difference between the Spectrum-X Ethernet multiplane and an off-the-shelf Ethernet solution can be as much as 400 times because of the mechanism by which that recovery is implemented in the Spectrum-X hardware.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: So the detection and then the restoration and rerouting of traffic adaptively to the alternate paths that exist in the multi-plane architecture is what gets to this result.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Versus either a software or similar driven recovery algorithm in order to be able to reroute traffic.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: So moving from scale out to now scale across. Spectrum XGS, which was announced some time ago, is a technology that NVIDIA has pushed forward in order to connect AI factories across regions, across geographies for multi-site distributed AI services.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: And. The key piece here is that it doesn't require a different switch. It's fundamentally in how the endpoints and the co-design of those endpoints and switches are orchestrated and managed.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Because ultimately, we don't really need deep buffers to be able to be the fail-safe in case of... We simply have to have smart crediting mechanisms between the endpoints in one data center and the others, so as to not bloat the latency through the scale across network.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: The transmission times are large anyway, so the last thing we would like to do is actually have deep buffers compound that problem. So with Spectrum-XGS, we are using a similar class of efficient, efficiently buffered switches, but using the endpoint and state exchange between those and between those clusters to be able to

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: drive consistent high throughput at low latency or at at minimum latency across those geographically separated AI clusters.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: So now moving to. Inside the compute node. BlueField, the BlueField DPU has now enjoyed wide deployment across AI factory infrastructure. And the primary model to date has followed the kind of client-server architecture, meaning that we were primarily binding tenants to GPU workloads.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: And. That's been a... A property or an attribute of cloud AI clouds for many years now is the flexibility to be able to do that. But in the era of agentic AI, this alone is actually not enough.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: The orchestration, the provisioning and the services associated with Agentic AI give the opportunity for Bluefield as a DPU to do so much more. in being able to provide the functionality for at scale agentic AI.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: There's a ton of diversity, but fundamentally, agentic workloads need to. run loops and be able to ingest particular types of models, determine which tenants are bound to those, and in the process of executing loops, dynamically introduce and enforce policy across all of the nodes that are

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: interconnected to that workload. So this is a very important function across storage, across CPU, across the scale out network. and even across the scale-across network. This orchestration.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: allows BlueField to be able to manage effectively a much higher surface of bandwidth than simply the throughput that is exiting. So while we used to call this. The front end network, it is much more than a front end network now.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: It is a scale in network where all the resources of the particular head node or the host are orchestrated and administered by the BlueField DPU. With the Astra technology that NVIDIA recently announced.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: The BlueField DPU effectively acts as a controlling DPU to all of the scale out supernics that are present in the actual. AI node. And so effectively the BlueField DPU has a scale-in element overall and enforces the policy on 7.2 terabits per second of throughput.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: Much higher than the actual throughput of your traditional front end NIC.

blocks.title: 幻灯片
blocks.speaker: Rochan Sankar

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: So we've talked about scale up, we've talked about scale out, scale across. context scale and scale-in. The basic message that I hope to leave you with today is that these aren't purpose-built infrastructures for the sake of being different.

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: They are optimized for the best possible performance, latency, power in each dimension of the Agentic AI infrastructure. And ultimately, their utility will be judged by how much better they can make the AI factory in terms of tokens per second and interactivity as the demands on those AI factories continue to scale much,

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: much higher in the years going forward. And so. We believe in this level of extreme co-design as being required between NIC and switch, between CPU and accelerator, between scale-up and scale-out and the various technologies that we've talked about today, and between hardware and software, ultimately, and system,

paragraphs.speaker: Rochan Sankar
paragraphs.text: in order to bring the most effective innovations for AI factories to bear and benefiting all of us. And thank you for your attention.

segments.title: 灵骏真武M890P超节点：MoE通信与负载均衡优化
segments.summary: 付斌章介绍M890P超节点网络及MoE推理优化。针对Dispatch与Combine、专家负载偏斜、通信同步开销和PD分离需求，说明磐脉互联与兼容接口，以及通信库、计算融合、零拷贝、专家均衡和细粒度重叠等协同优化。
key_points: 超节点在高带宽互联基础上兼顾PCIe、RoCE和应用通信接口。
Decode小消息强调减少同步与启动开销，Prefill大数据强调零拷贝和传输效率。
按Prefill与Decode不同节奏调整专家均衡，降低热点与尾部等待。
通信计算融合、细粒度重叠及广播去重策略随消息规模选择。

paragraphs.speaker: 桂新征
paragraphs.text: 下面有请阿里云智能集团高性能网络研发负责人付斌章，带来《灵骏真武M890P超节点网络优化实践》。掌声有请。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 大家下午好，我是来自阿里云的付斌章。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 今天非常高兴啊，有机会给大家介绍一下我们在过去几个月的一些工作。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那么首先呢我今天的这个报告呢大概分为3个部分。首先我可以给大家简单地回顾一下推理时代的通信挑战。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 我记得啊就在两个月之前，这是一个前OpenAI的这个研究员，叫Almeida，他发了一篇文章，他在文章中提到说2020年最原始的那篇Scaling Law论文存在一个bug，可能算错了，导致他这个结论出现了一些偏差。那么这篇文章出来之后呢，实际上大家就有一些这个讨论啊，就是说模型的尺寸是不是会继续的变大。那我想呢，经过这两个月的这样一个发展呢，这个事实呢已经给我们答案了。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那么最新的千问3.8 Max的我们的模型的尺寸呢已经达到了2.4T。那今天上午的时候呢，我们这个千问的这个负责人呢又发布了我们我们的模型的Roadmap，很快呢我们的模型呢就会达到这个10T的规模。那么模型的尺寸如此巨大，那么同时呢，如果说我们来看一下这个token的价格。那么按照前沿模型的每个Token的价格来计算的话，那么如果以2023年3月份的价格作为基线，那么到今年的这个2026年的9月份，那么我们每个 Token的前沿模型的Token的价格呢是2023年的16%，就下降了84%，那这个价格的下降是非常迅速的。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 换句话说呢，就是在推理场景下，就是不断的降低我们每个token的成本的价格，是我们这个业界广泛追求的这样一个目标。那但是呢对于这种超大的这种模型，特别是MOE架构的模型，它的尺寸是非常大的。那么优化它的这样一个性能和成本呢，实际上是一个非常挑战的这样一个事情。那根据我们的这样一个测算呢，就是在这种典型的这种超大尺寸的MOE架构的模型里面，它的端到端成本有50%实际上是消耗在通信上面。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那么，所以呢，今天我们就给大家一起讨论一下，就是如何来优化我们的这样一个通信的这样一个性能。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那么MoE模型它最大的优势就是说，它可以通过稀疏化的方式可以承载一个非常大的一个参数。但是呢它在真正在计算FFN的时候，它并不需要针对某一个token，让所有的专家都参与计算。它通过top K的方式选择K个专家来计算。那么典型的情况下，Top K的K值和我们的模型，模型的专家数量，是有数量级的差距，甚至达到两个数量级。通过这种方式呢，它可以既提供一个非常大的这样一个参数量，使我们的模型的这种能力表达能力非常强。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那同时又可以最小化我们的计算开销，使我们的成本达到最优。但是这种方式也不是完全没有成本的，那么因为我们需要去实时的去计算这个TopK的专家，哪些专家参与计算。那当我们算了之后呢，我们需要通过这种Dispatch的这种这种通信的机制呢，把这种Token送到这个相应的专家去计算。那在专家计算完之后呢，要通过Combine的这种通信的方式呢，把这个结果收集回来。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那么Dispatch和Combine这两个通信呢，实际上就带来了很多的这样一个开销。那除此之外呢，很重要的一点就是我们的这个这个topk的计算呢，是一个通过我们的一个门控网络来算的。它选择的专家实际上具有一定的概率性和随机性，就导致我们专家的负载非常不均衡。那么我们以这个通义千问3.8 Max为例的话，按照我们典型的这样一个在EP16的这样一个配置下，那我们可以看到这个最高负载的这个GPU，它的这个负载的这个这个程度呢，实际上是平均值的3.5倍。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那么这种极度的不均衡的这种负载呢，带来两个问题，一个呢就是这种负载高的GPU它的计算时间很长。那另外呢就是说因为你需要传出的这种Token的数量也很多，所以导致它的高负载GPU通信时间也很长。那我们知道我们这个这个推理任务实际上每一层的这种计算呢，它实际上隐含着一些同步的属性，那么这种高负载的GPU就会成为一个慢节点，导致我们整个推理任务的效率会大幅下降。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 另外呢就是说在我们现在的很多这种场景下，例如叫这种场景下，但是我们在Decode阶段的这种 batch size一般都会很小啊，典型值的话，像我们现在一般把Batch Size配到16，那么它的计算强度相对来说就会比较低。那么传统的这种two batch overlap这种方式呢，它是通过切分计算的方式来做流水线的Overlap。但是当你Batch Size比较小的时候，你切分，切分之后呢，因为计算强度下降了，实际上它计算时间并不能按线性的去减少，那会导致我们的这个最终的这个效果呢，反而是一个负向的一个优化。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那前面其实几个演讲嘉宾都提到了这一点，就是在推理时代可能PD分离呢是一个默认的一个配置。因为我们推理的它是一个典型的它有两个阶段，就一个Prefill和Decode。那么在Prefill阶段呢，因为它的 Input很长，所以它计算的量很大。那么这个时候它实际上是一个Compute-bound的任务。那么Decode阶段，因为它Input比较少，但是针对每一次计算，它要把KV Cache从存储空间里面Load到显存，所以它是一个显存带宽的一个bound的这样一个计算。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 这两种计算呢，实际上我一般需要把它分开部署，来避免它相互之间的干扰。那另外呢就是我们现在的集群呢，它一般倾向于每个集群里面部署的是相同的类型的GPU卡型。那所以说当我们用异构的这种卡型做PD分离的这种计算的时候呢，就会涉及到这种跨集群的这种高性能网络的通信，那同时就带来了很多RDMA通信的挑战。那这个挑战有几个方面啊，一方面就是我们KV cache流量是非常大的那我们测算下来之后，在千问3.8 Max我们的部署情况下，它的KV Cache流量峰值可以达到1.6 Tbps。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那这个峰值呢，实际上是我们这个机型的这个网卡的物理带宽的上限，并不是我们应用需求的上限。换句话说的话，如果说你的带宽可以更高的话，那他的KV cache流量的峰值带宽可以达到更高。但是呢我们在这种跨集群的这种长距离的RDMA传输的时候呢，我们传统的这种RDMA的这种协议技术呢，实际上并不能很好的适应。因为它的这个你的这个一旦涉及到长距的话，它就要上到这个广域网进行传输。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 刚才我们的Dennis和席永青已经提到了我们的eCore网络架构。那典型的这种骨干网呢，会给我们 RTT呢增加5~10毫秒的这样一个时延。这个时延的话，就导致我们的这种啊速率控制，包括我们的丢包率的上升，包括我们的重传的效率的下降。所以这个对RDMA的传输来说，带来了一个很大的一个挑战。那另外呢，就是这个我们的这个公平性。因为我们现在的这个集群里面会有多租户、有多任务，甚至是我们的训练任务、推理任务在混跑。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那这个时候呢，这种局部的拥塞也会导致我们这种这种相互之间的干扰，是吧？会影响其他任务的性能。所以说如何保证不同流量之间的性能QoS，也是我们现在面临的一个非常大的一个挑战。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: OK，那下面我来给大家简单介绍一下我们最新发布的灵骏真武M890P超节点。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 这个超节点呢和我们上一代的这个这个平头哥自研的PPU相比呢，它的无论它的这个算力，它的显存的容量，内存的容量，它的互联带宽都得到了很大的提升。这个超节点的话，它现在是规格呢是每个超节点是有64个GPU。它的互联带宽，整个实例的话，前端网络是3.2T，是通过DPU的方式来实现的。那Scale-out网络，整个实例可以达到12.8T的带宽。那Scale-up可以达到51.2TB的双向互联带宽。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那在这个超节点上面，我们现在配置的Scale-out网卡，是我们自研的这个磐脉 920，平头哥的自研的网卡。那这款网卡的话是400G的带宽，是两微秒的极致的一个时延。和普通的网卡不太一样的是，这张网卡内置了5.0版本的PCIe Switch。那它的好处就在于可以适配不同的计算平台。就是不管你的CPU里边的PCIe带宽是怎么样的，我们都可以保证GPUDirect RDMA性能的可预期稳定性。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那另外，我们这款网卡支持标准的RoCEv2，也支持我们这个阿里自研的这种Solar RDMA的这样一个协议。比较重要的是说我们可以做到QP级别的协议设置。那对应用来说的话，它是一个完全无感的，只需要在应用这个软通讯库在建立连接的时候呢，两边的网卡进行一个用户无感的一个协商，我们就可以确定这个QP使用哪一个协议。它的好处呢就是说它可以实现这种增量的，甚至是混合的部署。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那另外就是说当你使用了我们的SRD之后，我们就支持了包粒度的、PFC-free的多路径传输技术，以及我们自研的HPCC拥塞控制算法，以及最新的高通量以太网的一些新特性，后面会做一些具体介绍。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 这个是我们超节点的Scale-up网络，我们第一次使用了这种Switch架构的超节点架构，它通过一层ICN的Switch，可以把64个PPU完全连接起来，那每个PPU提供了800GB的双向互联带宽。然后我们的超节点现在在Scale-up网络里面也支持3种数据搬运方式，包括Load/Store内存语义的搬运，也包括AIU和Copy Engine的DMA消息语义的这种数据搬运方式。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 软件是非常重要的，就是为了大家能够非常丝滑地用起我们的超节点。就是我们现在阿里在大力打造的PPU开源软件生态。那在这个软件生态里面呢，就是我今天着重介绍的是和这个通信相关的。那我们现在对外开源了所有大家主流使用的这种通信的软件啊，包括这种集合通信。就是我们的PCCL的通讯库，那么它也支持了这种大家常用的，包括Reduce、All-to-all这些集合通信算子的接口，同时它也支持底层PCCL Gin的接口。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 这样的话，大家在这个自己的这个引擎里面也可以使用这种底层的接口，做数据的传输。那我们也支持了开源的DeepEP，包括V1和V2的版本。那比较重要的就是我们今天要讲的就是这个AcclMoE啊，是我们面向PPU超节点设计和研发的一款计算和通信融合的这样一个算子库。那么它支持多种量化格式，包括A8W8，A4W4。那么最大的也可以支持到这个64卡的这样一个规模。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那最后我给大家简单介绍一下，我们在超节点上的一个最佳实践，就是我们在超节点上部署千问3.8模型的一些趟过的坑啊，以及我们做的一些优化啊。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那首先先看一下，我们上一代的自研GPU实际上是没有超节点模式的，是吧？就是当我们需要这种千问3.8这么大的模型在部署的时候呢，它实际上是需要多台的这种服务器之间的这种这种部署，那它就涉及到我们的EP流量需要通过Scale-out网卡传输，它就带来这种带宽的瓶颈。在我们最新的M890P集群上面，那么因为我们这个是有64卡的一个 Switch的一个大的一个互联带宽域，那么这个时候我们就可以把这种带宽敏感的，包括TP并行和EP并行呢全部部署在我们的超节点内，那就可以享受这种超大带宽带来的这样一个红利啊。

blocks.title: 传统部署方式性能瓶颈分析
blocks.slide_title: 传统部署方式性能瓶颈分析
blocks.speaker: 付斌章

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那么首先看一下就是说为什么说传统的部署方式会带来很大的这样一个挑战呢？这个图实际上是我们在上一代的自研PPU上面部署千问3.8这样一个系统的Profiling图。那我们可以看到在pre-fill阶段啊，因为它传输的数据量很大，那么通信的端到端占比时间已经超过60%了。那另外呢，就是右边这个图呢，也可以看到它的通讯的负载的均衡度是非常差的，就是它这个高负载的和低负载的之间的差距，甚至达到几十倍啊。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那么我们大概统计了一下，由于负载不均衡导致的PPU空闲，导致我们的这个性能的吞吐的损失可以达到54%以上。那另外从左边图的下面我们也可以看到，就是在这种传统的这种方式下面，实际上我们的这种通信算子和计算算子之间呢，实际上是很难做overlap的，就基本上是一个串行的一个方式。那所以在通信的时候呢，实际上这个GPU的资源全部被浪费掉了。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那么由于时间的关系，今天我介绍的主要是面向Scale-up部分的一些优化工作，就明天上午就做个广告，明天上午还有一个平头哥的论坛，在那个论坛上我会介绍同样的工作，针对Scale-out优化的一些工作，也欢迎大家明天上午去平头哥的论坛啊，大家一起来讨论。在Scale-up这个Domain里面，我们首先优化的就是每一个通信算子的性能。那其实最有挑战的实际上是面向Decode的Low-latency算子，因为它的传输的数据量很小，那么我们会发现呢实际上它主要的开销来自于控制。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那么因为它本身每次发送，以PPU为例，每次发送完之后呢，你需要去做一次同步，那这个接收端呢才能确保数据已经被正确的写入了。那这个同步实际上是一个Grid System-level的同步，它的开销是很大的。那我们通过分析可以看到，控制的开销甚至大于数据传输的开销。那么优化这个这种小消息的传输呢，实际上就是要把这个控制的开销把它做到一个最小。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那我们使用的方式呢，就是把这个这个控制的这种消息呢，把它编码到我们的数据里面去。然后我们利用了底层GPU提供的128 Byte写数据的原子性，可以保证我们的数据和Flag一起写入。那这样的话，只需要接收端去。检查这个flag是否被置位，它就可以确定它这个这个数据是不是已经写到了，这样就避免了这样一个同步的这样一个操作。在典型的配置下，我们Dispatch的性能有百分之十几的提升。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那么在Prefill阶段，实际上是大数据的传输。那么大数据传输大家都知道，其实数据拷贝是大数据传输性能的主要的一个瓶颈。那所以我们针对Prefill阶段的通信算子，要做到零拷贝。那么我们在通信库里面对上层提供了一个可显式指定通信Buffer、可以把它Pin住的接口，扩展了这个API。那这样的话，上层的这个引擎呢，就实际上可以使用我们这个新的这种API接口来定义他自己的这个通信的缓冲区。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 这个缓冲区呢既可以用来做通信，也可以用来做计算啊，就是保证了他这个数据的这种完整性和正确性。那通过零拷贝的方式，我们在Prefill这里其实有30%、40%的这样一个性能的提升。

blocks.title: Qwen3.8-Max on M890P
blocks.slide_title: Qwen3.8-Max on M890P
blocks.speaker: 付斌章

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: Combine阶段的话，其实本质上讲，也是要做零拷贝，核心的原理是一样的。但是Combine会比Dispatch要复杂一些，因为Dispatch是纯数据的传输。但是Combine的话，它在收到数据之后还要做一次Reduce操作。所以说的话就不能做这种发送端的这种零拷贝，只能做这种接收端的。那我们的方式呢，就是说让接收端的这个这个SM通过load指令的方式，这也是我们的这个我们的超节点提供的这样一个最高效的一个数据传输的方式。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那通过这种load的指令的方式呢，把数据直接读到了这个接收端SM的寄存器里面，然后完成这种数据的计算，再写入到这种out buffer。通过这种通信和计算的零拷贝结合，那我们可以得到这种将近20%多的这样一个性能的一个提升啊。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 刚才也提到了，就是我们有54%的这种算力都有可能会损耗到，由于这个负载不均衡所导致的这样一个这种GPU的资源的一个浪费。那我们在超节点上尝试使用EP的负载均衡的这种一种机制。那这个原理呢其实很简单，就是说我们当我们发现某些GPU上面的这个专家负载比较高的时候我们就把专家的分布重新调整，让它更加均衡。但是专家的刚才也提到了我们的模型的尺寸越来越大，所以每个专家的这个这个搬迁的这个成本也很高。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 这个其实在我们传统的这种scale out网络上面其实是很难做的。就是它是一个得不偿失的，就是你你把这个专家搬过去，可能比你这个算一次的这个成本还要高。但是我们的M890P超节点给大家提供了一个超大带宽的一个scale up的网络域，所以给大家提供了这样一种可能性。但是呢它也不是说就是说完全的就是说你可以非常就是简单的去搬运。那么我们针对Prefill和Decode也采取了不同的方案，因为Prefill的计算这个这个时间比较长，因为它数据量比较大，所以它就相对来说可以容忍更加频繁的这种数据的这个专家的这种重分布。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 所以我们在Prefill阶段使用的是每一步都会在门控网络之后，我们有了明确的专家负载情况下，可以做非常精准的专家负载均衡调配。那么Decode阶段，因为它的计算量相对来说比较少，所以说它的计算时间比较短，它无法容忍这种频繁的这种专家的这种重分布，所以我们采用的方案呢是这种周期性的统计这种专家的这种负载。然后周期性的来做这种专家的重分布，通过这种方式的话，我们可以把这种不均衡的这种度从最高的啊3.37降到2.47。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 最后介绍一下我们的这个面向超节点的这种MoE的这个融合算子。这个融合算子是我们把FFN阶段的通信和计算融合在了一起。那通过这种方式的话，我们可以实现这个计算和通信的这样一个overlap，细粒度的overlap。那另外呢，刚才也提到了，我们支持了各种的这种量化的这种这种方式，以方便不同的模型啊接入到我们的这个这个这个库上面来。另外呢，就是说我们除了这个上面的算法之外的话，我们还做了很多Low-level指令级的优化，包括使用我们的AIU，AIU的话可能就是大家比较熟悉的话，就类似于这种TMA这种机制。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 还有我们的Copy Engine，BulkCopy，就是类似于Copy Engine的机制，我们可以通过这种硬件加速引擎啊，使得我们数据搬运的这个效率啊更高。那另外呢，就是我们还在这种针对不同的算子，我们使用了加冗余和去冗余的方式。这个就是听起来有点矛盾啊，就是为什么就是我们又要做去冗余是吧，又要加冗余呢？实际上这个呢，就是面向不同场景，我们采用的不同的这种方式。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那我们发现在这种小消息传输情况下，那么门控网络的这个时间呢，实际上是一个传统上想它是一个串行的，对吧？但是呢，我们发现数据量传得很少。但是我们如果去等这个门控网络把它数据算完，把这个结果算出来之后再去传呢，就会导致我们的时间都被浪费了。在这种情况下呢，实际上我们是一种冗余的机制，就是我们把这个数据呢就直接全传过去了，然后等到数据传到接收端的时候呢。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 门控的结果也出来了。那么这个时候呢，就是说它接收端直接可以根据这个路由的结果来取自己需要的Token来进行计算。那这是一个冗余的传输，哎，带来了这个这个性能的这样收益。那但是对于这种大块的数据传输呢，实际上我们就是要去冗余。因为我们发现一个GPU上面有很多个专家是吧？很多个专家可能收到的Token是相同的。那么如果你不去冗余的话，那这个Token就被发了很多份。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 那么在大数据量传输的时候呢，这个就会消耗我们很多的这种时间和带宽。那么在这种这种情况下呢，实际上我们是做的去冗余。那通过这些方式，我们可以达到端到端9%的性能提升。

paragraphs.speaker: 付斌章
paragraphs.text: 这个是最后的一个这样一个性能对比，我们这个对比了这种普通的这种PPU的节点，以及我们超节点上面的性能收益。那我们看到在千问3.8 Max，通过使用我们最新的超节点实例之后呢，Prefill呢有2.3倍的性能提升，然后Decode有1.1倍的性能提升。所以说这还是一个非常Exciting的结果，所以欢迎大家使用我们最新发布的PPU超节点，谢谢大家。

segments.title: 高质量Token：异构PD分离与算力网络的机会和约束
segments.summary: 章明星从内容质量与交付质量两方面解释高质量Token，讨论Chat、推理和Agent负载对Prefill与Decode资源比例的影响。结合Mooncake实践介绍异构算力利用、量化和运行时调度，并以跨楼宇异构PD实验说明网络带宽限制Prefill吞吐上限，而重叠可使TTFT基本不下降，进一步展望注意力压缩与跨地域算力池。
key_points: Token服务质量同时包含模型能力、首Token时延、逐Token时延、吞吐、稳定性和成本。
Prefill与Decode的算力和显存需求不同，异构资源分工可提升利用率。
量化校准、运行时重叠、调度及任务恢复是大规模部署的重要工程环节。
跨楼宇PD实验中，网络带宽约束Prefill吞吐上限，通过良好重叠可保持TTFT基本不下降；减少KV体量有助于跨域扩展。

paragraphs.text: 对，感谢邀请，刚刚大家也介绍了很多，包括PD分离，KV Cache复用，对网络的要求。其实我们现在在探讨的一个更多的事情就是未来我们显著会有更多的不同种类的这样的一些异构算力，但同时我们又需要很多的这样的一些所谓的高质量的Token，那我们让这两者之间怎么去更好的去衔接起来，是我们当下研究的这样的一个主题。这一页的内容其实不用太多，就是讲，就是基本上我们现在的中间的这一套推理系统的核心的目标，也就是将能源和算力转化为Token。

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 但这里面我们专门定义一个词叫做高质量的Token，它具体来说的话，其实我们可以细分为两个，一个就是这个Token内容的质量，也就是说这个模型它输出的Token的内容，它到底是好的还是不好的，基本上取决于你这个模型本身自身的能力。但除了这个模型自身的能力之外的话，其实我们额外会尝试去强调另外一种叫做交付质量的，就相当于是说你的输出的速度、你的稳定性、你的可靠性等一系列这块的交付质量，其实我们觉得在未来，特别是Agent这样的Workload下，是非常关键的一个内容，

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 而这里面最这个最显然的一点就是它的这个输出速度。就在早期，如果我们还是这样的一个简单的对话模型的这个场景下的话，那其实它的输出速度只要比这个人的看的速度要更快，其实就可以了。所以这大概就十几token就OK。但现在的话，对于coding的这个场景，其实我们可能需要30、40甚至50Token每秒的这样的一个输出速度，然后在未来大家现在也知道，现在叫无论是什么Loop Engineering的这样一些词，还是说RSI这样的一些词，或者说像OpenAI不是还解了千禧年的NS难题嘛，就是1万个Agent，然后同时来算88个小时，对这样一些场景，基本上我的这个交互性能要求越高越好，就是你的输出的速度，

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 那我怎么去供给这样的一个高质量的这个这个对应的这样的一个token，其实就是很核心的一个技术挑战。然后这里面的话，基础的PD因为刚刚讲了很多了，就我就快速的。

paragraphs.text: 过一下，就是它最核心的原理就是我们不要把这种高速的输出和我相对来说更看重这个吞吐的这个输入的throughput去混在一起，我们肯定是要把它自然的拆分到两个不同的这个环节里面。

paragraphs.text: 然后这块就不细聊了，我觉得核心还是说我们通过这样一个手段，其实我们最近发现就是其实大家之前对于异构PD这件事情是属于大家担心它会出问题，但是好像在具体的实践来看，好像又没有根本性挑战的这么一个状况，然后这个上半年的话我们就把这个。看起来没有根本性挑战，但实际做起来发现还是有很多这个工程性挑战，这个坑给全部都趟过去了。就比如说这个跨硬件的这个正确性，就所谓的这个就大家搞算子总要对精度，然后我们之前也是担心这个事情，然后后面发现就是KV Cache可能比如说现在因为大家做这个QAT啊，就是这个模型的量化，KV Cache 的量化其实还是相对比较成熟的一个状态。

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 所以虽然就是不同的异构的卡，它在这个精度转换上会稍微做一些变化，但是我们最终只要做一个比较好的这个Calibration的这个数据集。最后的结论就是说你的KV就保持8比特，不要去做极致的，比如说4比特甚至更低比特的这样的一个量化，其实整个精度是有保障的。然后在端到端的性能之上的话，大家其实之前更多的会担心的是你跨的这样的一个互联的网络，你的延迟的稳定性，你的网络会不会出问题。

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 但我们最后发现，其实很多时候它不一定卡在物理上，它很多的时候其实是卡在上层的这样的一些这个调度和一些这个Python的这个Runtime上。那如果说你把这块做得更好一点，比如说你重写一遍，或者说和其他的这个在线正在算的那个Batch做一个更好更极致的Overlap，其实这块的延迟大部分情况下是可以被 Overlap掉的，所以就是在TTFT的性能上，我们并不是特别的担心，然后最后其实就会回到这个生产可用性上，因为这个是一个非常极端的 PD比例，几十台往一台打，那你的这个网络的PFC或者说以及你开比较长的这个Pipeline Parallelism。

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 我们目前其实已经上线了千卡级别的国产异构PD分离的场景。当然我们正在，因为它本身的大框架是类似的，所以我们在快速的去扩展更多的不同的这样的一些显卡。

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 那么在这个基础之上的话，其实我们进一步会发现，如果说就在刚才的那个就是千卡规模的这个数据中心，其实我们还是单一数据中心里面放了多种不同的卡。那在这个建设的过程中，其实很核心的一个问题就是说你比例到底怎么配？以及说我们现在毕竟已经建设了这么多的数据中心，它很多它里面内部就是一个同构卡，那我有没有办法把它们给利用起来？以及刚刚我们也说，就是说不同场景下，它的PD比例在不断的变化，那如果我按照某一个特定的PD比例去配好了一个数据中心，然后PD比例变化了，那我是不是就完蛋了，我就出现了很多浪费的情况。

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 所以这里终归我们希望指向的一条路径，就是说我们真正把所有的算力变成一个更好的。弹性调度的一个更大的这样的一个池子，我能更灵活的去调度它，那就是我希望去做跨数据中心的这样一些PD的这样的一个混布。

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 那在这块的话，其实我们也做了一些简单的这个实验，就是我们现在很显然我们还没有办法做到说你真的是跨城市，真的是算力网的那个状态，但是说我们在一个园区，大家只是说不同楼中间还有专线互联的这种情况下。那我们去尝试说，那我网络条件可能没有那么好，我们也许未来我们可以做这个城域之间的RDMA的网络，那现在我们只能做一些跨楼的TCP网络，那在这种情况下，我们是不是足以去做到这样的一个这个跨楼的这样的一个PD分离的调度，

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 然后实验的结果发现还是目前还是比较乐观的一个状态，就首先可以看到通过这样的一个这个跨楼的PD分离，因为我们把decode的端从这个昇腾的芯片换成了H20的芯片，它的带宽有显著的提升。所以它的decode的这个时延其实是大幅度降低，那其实可以满足用户所谓高质量交付Interactivity的目标。

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 然后同时的话，我们发现就是我们基本上可以打满整个的这个网，这个TCP的网络带宽，以及在TTFT这件事情上，是目前从SLO的角度上是可以接受的。所以就大家可以看到这个呈现，就中间还有一条这个紫色的线，它是什么呢？其实就是我从物理和数学上，我直接可以算出来说，我对应这么多的PD传输的这个带宽，我能够的这个prefill的最高吞吐是多少？因为我做Prefill，它核心做的事情就是生产KV Cache，那我到底我生产KV Cache的这个上限，那肯定不能超过我的跨楼的这样的一个带宽，所以根据这个和特定的这个模型的架构，我就可以反推出来我配多少带宽，我最多的Prefill吞吐是多少，然后我们可以看到其实是可以打满的，

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 就相当于是你有多少带宽，我是可以给你压满，而且同时通过一个好的Overlap，我基本上是可以做到这个TTFT的不下降。那当然其实如果说你有更更好的带宽，在同构的情况下，目前你的PD其实是可以做到这个更高的这样的一个吞吐。但其实主要的原因是因为我们那个TCP专线拉得不够多，

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 所以后面我们正在做的事情就是拉更多的专线，让它的带宽进一步提升，然后同时等比地扩大我们的Prefill和Decode集群。那最后的目标其实也是希望我们至少两个同一个园区，两栋不同的楼，各自配千卡的这样的一个一个异构算力的规模，然后中间靠几条专线把它们拉起来。

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 特别是我们还可以看到最近DeepSeek V4.1 Flash还做了更加极致的KV Cache压缩，就是上周我还跟他们在算，就算完了之后，说不定真的是跨城的那个带宽都可以都可以去做了，就是我跨城做一个广域网，然后我只要做个SD-WAN，好像那个KV Cache其实都能传，要是真到了那个程度的话，那真的是这个全国八大算力中心可以连成一张网，然后里面想配什么算力就配什么算力，然后我想怎么去做全局的调度就怎么做全局的调度。

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 所以总体来说，我们对这件事情还是相对来说比较positive的一个一个状态。从这个大的模型的这个发展趋势来看，大家还是希望把KV cache去压低。然后另外一方面，虽然其实KV cache变小了之后，我们会希望说把context变长，但是因为context变长，它需要消耗的算力其实一般来说也是呈现一个超线性增长的状态。所以反过来，其实它对这个单位算力需要配的带宽，它不一定是增长，还是下降的趋势。

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 所以在这个可见未来，我们其实还是非常相信，就未来是真正可以去实现一个这个更多的异构算力去做一个综合的调度，让所有的算力都能充分利用的这样的一个一个状态。

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 然后前提当然是你做更好的一些焦点，而这是更多的一些数字上的计算，其实它跟刚才说的是一样的例子，就是在特定的KV Cache和算力配比下的话，你能做到一个什么样的状态？

paragraphs.speaker: 章明星
paragraphs.text: 对，就是对，这是我们目前发展的这样的一个一个路线图。就首先异构这件事情本身已经完全OK是可以上线的，只不过说我想大规模推广异构，它现在碰到了这个跨这个同数据中心去混布异构设备，它很多的这个部署上的难点。所以我们现在正在探索的就是跨楼的这样的一个异构。然后当我们的KV Cache压到一个更极致的状态的时候，我们其实未来就可能可以做一些更极致的这样一些跨区域的探索。
